claims.text: Rosacea care is matched to the features present (key point; also phenotype list intro)
claims.quote: Individual composition of clinical features guides treatment, ranging from mild monotherapy to combination therapies that address single or multiple elements through additional mechanisms

claims.text: More common in Northern European populations
claims.quote: affects males and females equally, with a predominance of disease occurring in Northern European populations.

claims.text: Common triggers include alcohol, spicy foods, sun exposure, and stress; triggers vary between patients
claims.quote: Common triggers include alcohol, spicy foods, sun exposure, and stress, but specific triggers vary between patients.

claims.text: Experts have not agreed whether rosacea patterns are separate entities or one spectrum
claims.quote: There remains a lack of consensus on whether varying subtypes of rosacea are individualized clinical entities or if they represent a spectrum of disease progression.

claims.text: No single treatment has been fully curative; rosacea is chronic (overview, FAQ 3)
claims.quote: Currently, no single treatment has been fully curative for rosacea

claims.text: Rosacea is a chronic condition (FAQ 3)
claims.quote: Rosacea is a common chronic dermatosis.

claims.text: The 2002 NRS classification described four subtypes
claims.quote: In 2002, the National Rosacea Society Expert Committee developed a subtype-based standardized classification system.

claims.text: ETR is the most common subtype in pooled estimates; four classic types (FAQ 2)
claims.quote: The proportions of those affected by rosacea were found to be 56.7% (95% CI, 51.4–62.0%) for erythematotelangiectatic rosacea (ETR), 43.2% (95% CI, 38.8–47.6%) for the papulopustular subtype (PPR), 7.4%

claims.text: Rosacea pustules show superficial neutrophils extending beyond the follicle, distinguishing from acne
claims.quote: Pustular lesions often show a superficial accumulation of neutrophils extending beyond the follicle, an important distinguishing factor from acne vulgaris.

claims.text: Chronic severe phymatous disease may need surgical or ablative laser treatment
claims.quote: Chronic and severe phymatous disease may require surgical therapy to remove excess tissue and recontour deformations. Procedural options include ablative lasers, electrosurgery, electrocautery, and dermabrasion.

claims.text: Ocular features: foreign body sensation, eyelid telangiectasia, chalazia, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, corneal ulcers
claims.quote: Foreign body sensations, eyelid telangiectasia, frequent chalazion, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, and corneal ulcers may be features of rosacea with or without cutaneous manifestation.

claims.text: People with eye involvement should be referred to ophthalmology to reduce risk of vision loss (subtype 4, key point, FAQ 11)
claims.quote: Patients with ocular involvement should be referred to ophthalmology to minimize the risk of vision loss.

claims.text: In 2017 the NRS Expert Committee moved to a phenotype-based approach
claims.quote: In 2017, the National Rosacea Society Expert Committee recommended a phenotype-based classification for therapy.

claims.text: Phenotype list: centrofacial erythema, major features, secondary burning/stinging/edema/dry appearance
claims.quote: groups pathognomonic centrofacial erythema with major phenotypic criteria—papules, pustules, flushing, telangiectasia, and ocular involvement. Secondary phenotypes include burning, stinging, edema, and dry appearance.

claims.text: Papulopustular rosacea often has background redness; combinations have outperformed monotherapy (clinical pearl)
claims.quote: Combinations such as topical metronidazole with subantimicrobial dose doxycycline and doxycycline 40 mg with daily application of ivermectin 1% cream are more efficacious than monotherapy with these agents.

claims.text: Combination therapy often used when features overlap (pearl, laser sequencing callout)
claims.quote: Combinative multimodal therapy is often utilized and required when treating patients with overlapping features of rosacea.

claims.text: Topical therapies have the highest level of evidence
claims.quote: the quality of evidence for available treatments varies depending on the modality, with topical therapies having the highest level of evidence.

claims.text: Most patients with papules and pustules can be treated with topical metronidazole, azelaic acid, or ivermectin
claims.quote: Most patients can be successfully treated with topical metronidazole, azelaic acid, or ivermectin.

claims.text: Ivermectin anti-parasitic against Demodex and anti-inflammatory, lowering IL-1 beta and TNF-alpha
claims.quote: It has anti-parasitic effects against D.and anti-inflammatory properties that increase IL-10 and decrease IL-1β, TNF-α, and neutrophilic activity.

claims.text: Metronidazole anti-inflammatory; used for papules, pustules and erythema (table row 'mild erythema')
claims.quote: Metronidazole contains anti-inflammatory properties and is used to treat erythema, pustules, and papules.

claims.text: Metronidazole 1% cream and 0.75% gel reduced lesion counts and erythema
claims.quote: Both 1% cream and 0.75% gel formulations reduced lesion count and erythema while also improving physician’s global rosacea scores

claims.text: Metronidazole tolerability improved with gentle cleanser, moisturizing, sunscreen
claims.quote: When metronidazole was combined with a gentle cleanser, hydration correction, and sunscreen, patient tolerability increased.

claims.text: Azelaic acid and antimicrobials lack evidence for isolated persistent redness
claims.quote: Other topical therapies, such as azelaic acid and antimicrobials, lack evidence in isolated persistent erythema.

claims.text: If not controlled after 8 to 12 weeks, a different topical or systemic agent may be considered
claims.quote: If desired symptomatic control is not achieved after 8 to 12 weeks of consistent daily use, a different topical agent or a systemic agent may be implemented.

claims.text: Doxycycline 40 mg is a sub-antimicrobial dose
claims.quote: The sub-antimicrobial dose of oral doxycycline (SDD) 40 mg has the strongest evidence and efficacy among oral therapies in the treatment of pustules and papules of rosacea

claims.text: Doxycycline 40 mg similar efficacy to 100 mg with fewer GI side effects
claims.quote: SDD, in comparison to doxycycline 100mg, was similar in efficacy with fewer adverse gastrointestinal side effects.

claims.text: Rosacea isotretinoin regimens use lower doses than acne dosing, including microdose, with lab monitoring and contraception
claims.quote: Continuous isotretinoin therapy in microdose form (0.04–0.11 mg/kg per day) may be a viable alternative, provided there is regular laboratory monitoring and adequate contraceptive measures for childbearing women.

claims.text: Demodex is a commensal mite; infestation more common in rosacea than healthy controls; many without rosacea carry it
claims.quote: The pooled prevalence of Demodex infestation was 70.4% in 1150 patients with rosacea compared to 31.8% in 1057 healthy controls (OR 9.04, 95% CI 4.83–16.93).

claims.text: Demodex antigens activate TLR-2 on keratinocytes; TLR2 highly active in rosacea
claims.quote: antigens propagate disease activity by sensitizing and activating TLR-2 on keratinocytes.

claims.text: Rosacea inflammation involves immune dysregulation, small vessels, microbiome, genetics, environmental triggers
claims.quote: Inflammation may be caused by dysregulation of proinflammatory cytokines (eg, IL-1, IL-3, and IL-8), alteration and dilation of small blood vessels, imbalances in the skin’s microbiome, genetic factors, and environmental triggers.

claims.text: Spicy foods trigger; TRPV1 hypothesis
claims.quote: which may be overexpressed in rosacea patients, and contribute to the characteristic flushing, warmth, and burning pain some patients may experience.

claims.text: Heat exposure and exercise associated with rosacea; alcohol and stress triggers
claims.quote: Sun/heat exposure, alcohol consumption, exercise, and stress represent environmental factors that have also been associated with an increased risk of rosacea

claims.text: A trigger journal can help identify triggers
claims.quote: A journal can be used to identify possible triggers and additional strategies.

claims.text: Mild ocular disease: artificial tears and lid hygiene
claims.quote: Milder presentations of disease can be managed with artificial tears and adequate lid hygiene.

claims.text: Oral doxycycline frequently used for ocular rosacea
claims.quote: Doxycycline is also frequently used to treat ocular rosacea.

claims.text: Lasers and IPL treat flushing, redness, telangiectasia though evidence is narrow
claims.quote: Although the quality of evidence is narrow, light therapies and lasers have been successful in the management of rosacea features, particularly telangiectasias and phymatous change.

claims.text: PDL light selectively absorbed by oxyhemoglobin (selective photothermolysis)
claims.quote: PDL uses visible (yellow) light that is selectively absorbed by oxyhemoglobin, a process known as selective photothermolysis.

claims.text: PDL 585 to 595 nm; targets vascular component and reduces Demodex density
claims.quote: PDL aims to address the photodamage response by targeting both the inflammatory vascular component of rosacea while reducing Demodex density.

claims.text: IPL delivers multiple wavelengths at once
claims.quote: IPL, which is characterized by multiple wavelengths emitted simultaneously with an optic cutoff filter that selects the spectral output.

claims.text: KTP especially effective for telangiectasia
claims.quote: Consequently, it is remarkably effective for telangiectasia treatment.

claims.text: Nd:YAG designed for deeper, darker vessels; used for diffuse facial redness (also framework table)
claims.quote: Though originally designed to target deeper and darker vessels and allow for ideal thermal relaxation time, Nd:YAG is effective in the treatment of diffuse facial erythema.

claims.text: CO2 and Er:YAG lasers for phymatous rosacea
claims.quote: (CO) and erbium: yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Er:YAG) lasers are also helpful in treating phymatous rosacea.

claims.text: Procedures need meticulous care and training to avoid lasting damage
claims.quote: Each modality requires meticulous care and a proficient level of training due to risks associated with permanent damage and dysfunction of treated areas.

claims.text: Rhinophyma can recur after surgical procedures
claims.quote: Rhinophyma can recur following surgical procedures and may require further revision.

claims.text: Framework table: combination ivermectin plus doxycycline for papules and pustules
claims.quote: doxycycline 40 mg with daily application of ivermectin 1% cream are more efficacious than monotherapy with these agents.
